speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. To better understand what's going on, can you tell me when this pain started and if it follows any specific activity or movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. Given the radiation of pain to the elbow and your mother's history of autoimmune joint disease, have you noticed any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes or swelling in your knuckles? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray right wrist and elbow.

speaker: Doctor

I have reviewed your initial labs and imaging; please describe precisely how you hold your infant's hand that causes the most pain, and tell me if you have noticed any numbness or tingling in your thumb, index, or middle fingers.

REQUEST TEST: Nerve Conduction Study (right upper extremity).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal nerve conduction study and your mother's history of rheumatoid arthritis, I am concerned about an inflammatory joint issue. Did you notice any visible swelling or deformity in your right thumb base (carpometacarpal joint), and does pressing on the first knuckle of your thumb cause sharp pain? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right hand and wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis of the right first carpometacarpal joint.
